It is designed for users who want a high-quality skill package rather than a minimal draft. It can help create new skills, strengthen existing ones, complete artifacts such as README and evals, improve trigger boundaries and workflows, and safely refine locally available skills after access and editability checks.

latestVersion.changelog:
Compared with the previous version, this release includes:

- Clarified the core capability set so users can see more easily that `skill-enhance` supports not only skill creation, but also skill enhancement, local skill customization, and publish-readiness review.
- Improved the public-facing description and metadata so the skill is presented more clearly as a quality-first skill, not just a minimal draft generator.
- Reworked `README.md` so it reads more naturally as a GitHub project overview, focusing first on what the skill is, who it is for, how to use it, and what it produces.
- Strengthened the usage boundaries so users can more easily understand when `skill-enhance` is the right tool and when it is not.
- Improved the example prompts and explanatory wording so users can get started faster and better understand practical cases such as local skill optimization and release review.
